claims.statement: ChatOpenAI is the primary class in langchain-openai that wraps OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs, with support for structured output, tool calling, vision, streaming, and model profiles.
OpenAI API key can be provided as a string, sync callable, or async callable; if not provided, it is inferred from OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.

Base URL for API requests resolves in order: explicit base_url kwarg, OPENAI_API_BASE environment variable (read by LangChain), OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable (read by OpenAI SDK). When base_url is set, stream_usage is disabled by default because many non-OpenAI endpoints don't support streaming token usage.

ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output() supports three methods: 'function_calling' (tool-calling API, default), 'json_schema' (OpenAI Structured Output API for strict conformance), and 'json_mode' (JSON mode without strict schema validation).

bind_tools() binds one or more tools to the model and accepts tool_choice parameter to specify 'auto', 'none', 'any'/'required', a tool name string, or a dict specifying which tool(s) to call. It also supports parallel_tool_calls, strict, and response_format parameters.

tool_choice supports 'auto' (default), 'none' (prevent tool use), 'any'/'required'/True (force at least one call), a tool name string (force specific tool), WellKnownTools strings like 'file_search' and 'web_search' (built-in tools), and dict format for OpenAI's native tool choice specification.
The parallel_tool_calls parameter controls whether the model can call multiple tools in a single response. Defaults to None (allow parallel). Set to False to enforce sequential tool calls.
Streaming output integrates with LangChain callbacks; on_llm_new_token() is invoked for each token chunk via run_manager, with per-chunk metadata passed to custom callback handlers.

stream_chunk_timeout is a per-chunk wall-clock timeout for async streaming (default 120 seconds); it measures silence between parsed chunks (not inter-byte silence), and can be disabled via LANGCHAIN_OPENAI_STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_S environment variable.
Vision is supported on gpt-4-vision, gpt-4o, and gpt-4-turbo models; images can be provided via image_url with detail parameter ('low', 'high', 'auto') or as base64-encoded data URIs.

Model profiles are auto-generated metadata stored in _profiles.py describing capabilities: text/image/audio/video inputs/outputs, max tokens, tool calling, structured output, tool_choice, and tool_call_streaming support.

ChatOpenAI targets official OpenAI API specifications only; non-standard response fields added by third-party providers (e.g., reasoning_content, reasoning_details) are not extracted or preserved. For provider-specific features, use provider-specific packages (e.g., ChatDeepSeek, ChatOpenRouter).

ChatOpenAI automatically switches between Chat Completions API and Responses API based on model name, parameters, and explicit configuration; Responses API is used when reasoning, context_management, truncation, include, or use_previous_response_id are specified, or when model name starts with 'gpt-5' (pro variants) or model is 'codex'.

Responses API supports streaming reasoning for reasoning models, structured output with tools, context management via context_management parameter for automatic message compaction, truncation strategy control, and previous response tracking via use_previous_response_id for conversation continuity.

ChatOpenAI maps OpenAI SDK exceptions to LangChain's standardized error hierarchy: AuthenticationError -> ModelAuthenticationError, PermissionDeniedError -> ModelPermissionDeniedError, BadRequestError (context_length_exceeded) -> ContextOverflowError, RateLimitError -> ModelRateLimitError, NotFoundError -> ModelNotFoundError, APIError -> ModelAPIError, APIConnectionError -> ModelConnectionError, APITimeoutError -> ModelTimeoutError.
Automatic retries for transient failures (429, 500-599) are configured via max_retries parameter; request timeout is controlled via timeout parameter (float or tuple of connect/read timeouts).

BaseChatOpenAI initialization resolves API authentication from parameters/environment variables/callables, builds HTTP clients (sync and async) with optional socket options, registers model profiles, validates parameters like stream_chunk_timeout, and initializes OpenAI client instances.
When an async callable is provided for api_key, the sync client is not available; sync methods (invoke, stream) raise ValueError, requiring use of async methods (ainvoke, astream) instead.

AzureChatOpenAI is a subclass of BaseChatOpenAI that inherits all ChatOpenAI functionality (tool calling, structured output, streaming, vision) but with Azure-specific authentication (azure_endpoint, api_key, azure_ad_token), endpoint routing via azure_deployment, and API versioning (api_version distinct from model version).

AzureChatOpenAI responses include Azure-specific metadata: prompt_filter_results and content_filter_results in response_metadata detailing content safety filtering for hate speech, self-harm, sexual content, and violence.

ChatOpenAI converts LangChain message types (HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage, ToolMessage) to OpenAI API format and back; output is AIMessage with content, tool_calls, invalid_tool_calls, additional_kwargs (audio, function_call), response_metadata (token usage, finish reason, system fingerprint, logprobs), and usage_metadata (standardized token counts).

For multi-modal content, ChatOpenAI formats content blocks per API requirements; Chat Completions API filters certain block types (thinking, tool_use, reasoning_content, and function_call/code_interpreter_call when on Chat Completions API), while Responses API expands support for reasoning, computer use, file search.

ChatOpenAI can be subclassed to customize behavior via overriding _generate, _stream, _agenerate, _astream methods; custom middleware can be added via RunnablePassthrough, RunnableLambda, or decorator patterns.

OpenAIDecisions is a RunnableSerializable that asks Predicate (probability), Choice (selection), and Score (multi-level) questions about text, images, or messages via OpenAI's Decisions API, returning typed answers with probabilities, confidence, and token usage.

DecisionRequest contains input (text/messages/state) and a dict of named Question objects; DecisionResponse returns dict of typed Answer objects (PredicateAnswer with probability, ChoiceAnswer with choice/probabilities/confidence, ScoreAnswer with score/legend/probabilities/confidence, RefusalAnswer), plus usage and request_id.
Predicate questions estimate the probability (0.0-1.0) that a condition is true; PredicateAnswer contains probability field used for binary gates, risk assessments, or eligibility checks.

Choice questions select one value from a fixed, unordered set of options; ChoiceAnswer contains the selected choice, probability distribution over all choices, and confidence (0.0-1.0) representing distribution concentration, not the choice's own probability.

Score questions rate input against ordered levels (e.g., Low/Medium/High); ScoreAnswer returns score (probability-weighted average of zero-based indices, may be fractional), legend (level labels keyed by index), probability distribution, and confidence.

OpenAIAutoModeMiddleware intercepts configured tool calls, asks a Predicate risk question via the Decisions API, and blocks calls with probability ≥ 0.5 by returning an error ToolMessage without execution; low-risk calls execute normally.

OpenAIAutoModeMiddleware's default risk instructions ask whether execution would be risky or insufficiently authorized, covering destructive actions, credential access, external sharing, security bypasses, persistence, protected-resource changes, and unauthorized actions; only explicit user messages authorize execution.

OpenAIAutoModeMiddleware includes base64 images in Decisions requests but replaces audio, video, and file content with placeholders ([audio omitted], [video omitted], [file omitted]); if images are rejected (HTTP 400 or 413), retries with all images replaced.
OpenAIAutoModeMiddleware sends up to 30 recent messages, the proposed tool call (id, name, args), and tool description in a structured dict to the Decisions API for risk classification.

OpenAIAutoModeMiddleware returns blocked tool call messages: 'The tool call `<name>` was blocked because it was classified as risky (probability: X.XX)' for high-risk calls, or 'was blocked because its risk could not be assessed' when the model refused.

OpenAIModelRouterMiddleware classifies the latest HumanMessage once before agent execution using a Choice question, stores the route (selected model, probabilities, confidence) in agent state, and routes all subsequent model calls to the selected model.

OpenAIModelRouterMiddleware falls back to the agent's own model if routing fails (model refuses, no human message exists, or API error); when model_route is None, model calls use the agent's default model.

OpenAIModelRouterMiddleware includes base64-encoded images in routing decisions but replaces hosted image URLs, files, and audio with placeholders; if images are rejected (HTTP 400 or 413), retries with all images replaced.

decide_with_text_fallback() and adecide_with_text_fallback() retry Decisions API requests with images on HTTP 400 or 413 errors, ensuring that image issues do not block guardrails or routing; middleware degrades gracefully to text-only assessment.
